05 — What remains when the project ends: the pack cycle

Tutorial 04 closed MeuApp's RN-001 delivered and validated. The project is done — features delivered, validate green, the client satisfied. And now? What MeuApp leaves behind is not just code: it is maturity — the patterns that worked, the metrics the evals measured, the fine lessons the team learned, the domain knowledge that was researched. This tutorial asks a single question: where does that maturity live, and how does it reach the next project?

The answer has a name: the pack. And a complete cycle, which this doc walks from start to end: the project closes → the retrospective extracts → the pack accumulates → the publish pushes → the org repo keeps → the next project inherits.

1. Create the pack repo in the organization (once per org)

Maturity is an organizational asset — so it lives in a Git repository of its own owned by the org, not in a loose folder on your computer. Create the private repo (on the GitHub UI or with the CLI):

gh repo create <org>/<pack-repo> --private

The name is up to you — what matters is: private repo, owned by the org, with room to grow. This repo is the source of truth of the organization's maturity: everything the projects reveal goes up here.

2. Create the pack (the first time)

With the repo created, the gm-pack-scaffold skill assembles the full pack skeleton from the FORMAT §3.1 contract — the initial commit and the canonical structure:

pack.yaml                    # the pack manifest (kind: state — bidirectional working copy)
README.md                    # the pack's purpose
skills/                      # skills/agents the org shares by overlay
rules/                       # the org's norms (one per file, with a trigger)
domains/                     # the domain foundation (KNOWLEDGE.md per domain)
accumulation/                # the accumulated learning:
├── patterns/                #   the reusable patterns (by type: code, process…)
├── metrics/                 #   the project metrics accumulated over time
└── nuances/                 #   the fine observations, one per theme

What each part is: pack.yaml declares what the pack provides and the archetype (kind: state — the clone is a bidirectional working copy, not a read-only cache). rules/ and domains/ are declarative knowledge — the house way and the domain understanding. accumulation/ is the accumulated learning — every project deposits here and the pack keeps the history.

3. Link it on your machine

golmet pack add <repo-url> --engine opencode

The kit clones the repo into <config>/packs/<id>/ — the bidirectional working copy: it is linked to the repo (origin points at it) and the kit knows that is a pack, not a loose file. From here, the org's maturity is available on your machine: the triggered norms enter the AGENTS.md, the patterns become visible to the skills.

4. The retrospective (every time a project closes)

MeuApp closed. Before archiving, run the gm-project-retrospective — the skill that conducts the extraction of what the project revealed, with the canonical writers recording into the pack's working copy:

  • the patterns that worked → accumulation/patterns/<type>/, by the gm-pattern-extractor (a pattern = the problem, the solution and the code demonstrating it);
  • the retrospective metrics (coverage, evals, what was measured) → accumulation/metrics/, by the gm-metrics-collector;
  • the fine observations ("the scheduler drifts 2s against the confirmation database") → accumulation/nuances/<theme>.md, by the gm-nuance-collector — one nuance per theme, append-only;
  • the domain knowledge the project researched → domains/, by gm-domain-research (when founded — primary sources with URL and access date).

Each writer has its own format and trigger — and the knowledge router (docs/concepts/knowledge.md) decides the destination when the artifact has no obvious one.

5. Push to the org repo

golmet pack publish

The publish performs the WIP commit (the working copy's uncommitted changes) and the push to the org repo — the source of truth of the maturity, updated. The rule is deliberate: the publish is manual by design — the operator decides when the knowledge is ready to be shared (nothing goes up without your hand; the kit never discards what the team accumulated, but it also never publishes without a decision).

6. Inherit

The org's next project (or a new collaborator's fresh machine): golmet pack add again — and the accumulated maturity is there immediately: the house norms, the patterns MeuApp left, the domain foundation. For those who already have the pack linked: golmet pack update syncs the repo into the working copy (with auto-commit of the local accumulation and rebase — never discarding what you have).

Golmet matures with use: the first project teaches; the second inherits.

The cycle, from above

   project closes (validate green, deliveries done)
          │
          ▼
   gm-project-retrospective ── extracts (patterns · metrics · nuances · domains)
          │                          records INTO THE PACK'S WORKING COPY
          ▼
   golmet pack publish ── WIP commit + push (manual by design)
          │
          ▼
   organization repo (e.g. <org>/<pack-repo>) ── the source of truth
          │
          ▼
   golmet pack add (the next project · the new machine) ── inheriting

What this cycle buys the organization: the second project starts with the house norms in place, the proven patterns available and the domain foundation researched — the team's AI inherits the house way on day one.

The journey ends — the cycle continues
